answer: Every new identity has to earn a work ticket. The applicant submits a public key and hardware fingerprint, and the network hands back a puzzle tied to that key. The first identity from one machine is cheap, eight minutes on a laptop, but the difficulty doubles for each extra identity sharing the same fingerprint, so a hundred fakes costs weeks of compute. Solved proofs get anchored on chain with an expiry date; misbehaving identities lose the anchor and start over. One honest agent is a single plume of smoke; a sybil farm faking a thousand islands just chokes on its own exhaust.
